news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

French protests over the education and the cost of living have turned into widespread looting of major luxury stores — with rioters hitting Louis Vuitton, Hermes, and Apple.

Some designer brands, such as Dior, have reportedly hired private security teams to protect their stores in Paris after French police appeared to lose control of the streets of the capital.

More than 1,800 people have been arrested and President Emmanuel Macron addressed the nation, vowing to track down the looters who are trying to “bring down the Republic.”

Mobs looted the Galeries Lafayette — a luxury department store in Paris akin to Bergdorf Goodman or Harrods — with gangs of masked thugs seen smashing storefronts and raiding shelves on Saturday.

A picture showing a robust private security crew hired to protect a flagship Dior store in Paris went viral online.

In Marseille, looters targeted luxury brand Hermes, as well as stores selling jewelry, makeup and clothes.

Fire crews in the city said they had to put out a blaze that began in a designer shoe store.

In Bordeaux, a masked crowd was seen breaking down the doors to a Louis Vuitton store, as a parade of protesters waved red flags with hammer and sickle signs along the street.

In Lille, an Apple store was vandalized and looted, while in Nice, sportswear outlets and a motorcycle dealership were stormed.

Unrest broke out in France several weeks ago ostensibly as a student protest, but quickly devolved into an orgy of looting and riots.

Many other groups, including leftists and pro-Palestinian fanatics, have also used the riots as an excuse to force their agendas.

Dior had no faith in the French police to protect their store so they brought in their own security team to protect the flagship store in Paris tonight pic.twitter.com/aShDIzBeHS

Some 1,800 people were arrested on Saturday nationwide, while more than 500 cops were injured.

Rioters have also targeted France’s cultural heritage, with thugs torching the 140-year-old city hall in the southern city of Limoges, while Lyon’s tourist office was also set on fire.

Addressing the nation on Sunday, French President Macron said that “nothing justifies” the violence his country has seen this weekend.

“Tonight, we all feel anger and shame,” Macron said in the televised address, drawing a distinction between protesters with “legitimate demands” and “those who destroyed, smashed and looted.”

He said the looters “will have to pay back for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable.”

Macron blamed the “unrestrained violence” on “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.”

It comes after Vice President J.D. Vance blamed mass immigration for the violent scenes in France.

“Western liberals imported the Third World into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this, and they didn’t listen,” he wrote on X.

“I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” Vance added.

Former NFL player and TV personality Damien Woody shared a surprising health update with fans in an Instagram post on Sunday.

The former Jets offensive lineman, who left ESPN two months ago, revealed that he has been hospitalized after having his appendix and part of his colon removed following a colonoscopy.

“Want to give folks a health update,” Woody wrote. “Had a colonoscopy and from that have been hospitalized after having had my appendix and part of my colon removed. I want to thank all the doctors and nurses at Morristown Medical Center for the tremendous care I received. For the masses…mmm please get your checkups! Life is too short and too precious.”

The former Jets offensive lineman left ESPN two months ago after the network didn’t renew his contract in August. This ended his 15-year tenure as an NFL analyst.

Woody, a two-time Super Bowl champion with the Patriots, did not have his ESPN contract renewed after it expired in August, ending his 15-year tenure with the network.

Woody is now part of “The OG Football Show” on YouTube with fellow former ESPNers Trey Wingo, Mark Schlereth and Merril Hoge.

Woody announced his retirement from the NFL on July 26, 2011. Less than two weeks later, he made his ESPN debut. Over the years, Woody grew as an on-air personality and became a key contributor on “SportsCenter,” “NFL Live,” “Get Up,” “First Take” and other ESPN programs.

“Being a guy who had a serious speech impediment to working on tv was truly one of my proudest accomplishments. Looking forward to what God has in store for me next!” Woody said about his departure.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Lefty incumbent state Attorney General  Letitia James’ lead over GOPer Saritha Komatireddy has shrunk to just 6 points after the underdog’s strong debate performance, a bombshell Republican internal poll shows.

James now leads Komatireddy by just 50.7% to 44.7% — half of the Democratic AG’s 13-point spread in a Siena University survey last month, according to the new poll conducted for the GOP candidate and obtained by The Post.

About 4% of voters remain undecided, the latest survey found.

An analysis of the findings suggested that the Republican well-regarded former federal prosecutor’s Oct. 8 debate performance is largely responsible for shrinking the gap and provided her with momentum for her uphill battle in deep-blue New York during the home stretch.

“Letitia James sits at 50.7% with her negatives rising; Saritha Komatireddy is at 44.7% with a +15 net image,’’ wrote the GOP campaign’s pollster, OnMessage Inc., said in an Oct. 15 memo.

“The final three weeks are about one thing: putting Saritha in front of the voters who have not seen her yet, because the  ones who saw her debate are breaking to her by four to one.’’

One in five likely voters  surveyed said they watched the  debate.

Among those who watched, Komatireddy scores with them 81% to 19%. the poll showed.

Among the voters who did not watch the debate, James bested her foe 59% to 36%.

“That gap is the whole campaign in one number: the undecided and soft voters who see Saritha make the case against James move to her, and the ones who have not seen it stay with the incumbent simply by default,” OnMessage said.

OnMessage  surveyed 1,000 New York likely voters from October 12–14, with the poll having  a  margin of error of 2.8 percentage points.

Registered independent voters have shifted to Komatireddy, the survey added..In May, James was +3 with independents — 40% favorable, 37% unfavorable with the rest on the fence.

Now, James is 11 percentage points underwater with non-party-affiliated voters — 40% favorable to 51% unfavorable, with many  saying “very unfavorable.”

Komatireddy now leads James among independents 49% to 43%.

”This is where a well-funded closing message makes the difference,” the GOP pollster said.

Komatireddy is winning areas where Republicans need to perform well.

She leads James on Long Island 57% to 41% and the broader downstate suburbs 54% to 44% and upstate 50% to 44%.

James is ahead because of her huge margin in New York City, where she bests Komatireddy 65% to 30%.

Komatireddy leads among men 53% to 43%,  non-college voters 50% to 45%, and in terms of voters ages 46 to 55, 51% to 46%, according to the survey. The memo did not specify James’s lead among women.

The analysis noted that James only defeated underfunded Republican challenger Michael Henry by 9 percentage points when she won her second term in 2022.

But Komatireddy will have to peel away some soft or persuadable James backers to pull off an upset, the pollster noted.

Polling analyst Nate Silver gave OnMessage an A rating as one of the most accurate pollsters during the 2024 election cycle.

As a federal prosecutor in Brooklyn’s Eastern District of New York, Komatireddy handled some of its most high-profile cases involving international terrorism, cybercrime, narcotics trafficking, money laundering, and public corruption.

James has meanwhile filed numerous lawsuits to block controversial actions taken by the Trump administration, including for allegedly providing energy companies $1.4 billion in funds to cancel four critical offshore wind projects, and on other funding and policy issues.

James has garnered nationwide attention for prosecuting Trump and his namesake company for fraudulent practices.

“Saritha Komatireddy wouldn’t protect New Yorkers from fraudsters or the federal government, because they’re the ones propping up her candidacy,’’ a James campaign spokeswoman told The Post on Sunday when asked about the new poll.

“Trump endorsed her, and she’d repay him by looking the other way while he sows chaos in New York.”

James  also commissioned a sexual misconduct probe of ex-Gov. Andrew Cuomo that triggered the Democrat’s resignation from office in 2021, even as he denied wrongdoing.

“There has been a tremendous surge of interest in Saritha and her vision for New York since her overwhelming debate victory over Ms. James,’’ said Saritha for New York campaign manager Isabelle Daigle to The Post.

“We’re seeing Democrats and independents joining with Republicans all across the state because of Saritha’s no-nonsense, apolitical approach to crime, homelessness, and fraud.

“Our polling data is internal, but we’re happy to report that we have extraordinary momentum on our side going into the final two weeks of this election. We like where we are, while understanding that we will have to work twice as hard to earn the individual votes of New Yorkers of all backgrounds over the next 15 days.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

WASHINGTON — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent knocked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for publicly accusing the Trump administration of throttling his country’s access to a military version of Starlink, which is critical for battlefield communications.

Zelensky alleged that someone in the administration gave orders to slow down satellite internet in objects cruising at 160 km/h or more, which undermined Kyiv’s drone operations.

“President Trump and Secretary Rubio have categorically said that no one in the Trump administration did that,” Bessent told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday. “And I think it is very reckless for President Zelensky to make such a charge.”

“I don’t know anything about that, but we’ve been very clear. And, you know, President Zelensky should be very careful about making statements like this that aren’t true.”

The mystery surrounding the limiting of Ukraine’s Starshield access has been dominated by confusion and finger-pointing.

Initially, top Ukrainian and European officials blamed near-trillionaire tech guru Elon Musk for curbing “Starlink” access. But Musk later claimed it was the military version of Starlink known as Starshield that was throttled and indicated it came from the Trump administration. Musk and a top Ukrainian official also suggested it was being restored.

However, Zelensky said in a prerecorded interview that aired on NBC’s “Meet the Press” Sunday that the limit was still in effect.

“We [still] have [a] limitation. The speed is [a] maximum [of] 161 kilometers. Not miles, kilometers,” he said.

The slowing down of Starshield access came as President Trump was pressuring Ukraine to back down on its drone strikes on Russian energy targets.

Both Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that the administration ordered the throttling, though a report from Reuters claimed that someone in the administration ordered it.

“Of course, the message came from government. I don’t know from whom, what cabinet, and et cetera. And I think it doesn’t work either way,” Zelensky said. “But it’s not my opinion. It’s [the] opinion of our generals, of our government.”

Around the time that the throttling was revealed, Zelensky claimed that the US stopped sharing critical intelligence with Ukraine about incoming ballistic missile attacks from Russia, something he said has since been reversed.

Bessent also defended Trump’s decision to ease up on sanctions regarding Russian diesel and postpone implementation of Russian sanctions included in a bi-partisan bill named after the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.

“The only thing that has been lifted is the diesel embargo. And, you know, I will point out the UK in May waived their embargo on diesel and jet fuel made with Russian crude,” Bessent said.

“Where’s the outrage for the rest of the world? President Zelensky does not criticize his European partners,” he added. “The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine. The US imports $4 billion of Russian products. One-point-eight billion of that [is] fertilizer. Europeans import more than ten times that.”

Zelensky had talks with US special peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on Sunday amid the souring relations and posted that peace would only come through “cooperation built on trust.”

Had a conversation with the American President’s envoys, Steve Witkoff @SEPeaceMissions and Jared Kushner @jaredkushner. Peace comes only through strength and cooperation built on trust. We are doing everything on our part to make this happen, and to ensure that America’s… pic.twitter.com/eNFwsJkNJS

Trump’s diesel deal with Russian strongman Vladimir Putin came as he grapples with midterm headaches due to high prices of the fuel that is heavily used by farmers.

The Treasury secretary also stressed that the Trump administration has enacted aggressive sanctions against Russia since the president took office in January of last year.

“First of all, the sanctions were doubled. The Biden administration, in an act of incredible bravery,” Bessent said sarcastically, “doubled the sanctions on the way out, in January of 2025. But we did not take those down.”

“President Trump sanctioned the two largest Russian energy companies, Rosneft and Lukoil, which dealt a catastrophic blow to the Russian energy industry,” he went on. “So no one has been tougher on Russian sanctions than President Trump.”

As Williams and the 49ers are set to take on the Washington Commanders on Monday night, Williams admitted that he forgot he played there.

Trent Williams is nearing the end of a illustrious 16-year career and has appeared to have forgotten the first half of it.

As Williams and the 49ers are set to take on the Washington Commanders on Monday night, Williams admitted that he forgot he played there.

#49ers OT Trent Williams, asked if he’ll have any mixed feelings playing Washington after spending the first 9 years of his career w/ them:“Sometimes I forget that I even played there. … I’ve (spent almost) as much time here as I did there.” pic.twitter.com/aZaj36AuXm

“Sometimes I forget that I even played there. I only played nine seasons there,” Williams told Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle on Saturday. “It’s been almost as much time here as I have there.”

Williams’ career began with the Commanders after he was selected by the team with the No.4 overall pick of the 2010 NFL Draft.

From 2012-2018, Williams was selected to seven consecutive Pro Bowls and helped Washington reach the playoffs in 2012 and 2015.

During the 2019 season, Williams was placed on Washington’s non-football injury list and missed the entirety of the year.

In 2020, he was granted permission to seek a trade and would end up being traded to the 49ers in exchange for a fifth-round pick of the 2020 NFL Draft and a third-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.

While Williams has appeared to have forgotten about his time in Washington, the team hasn’t.

In 2022, Williams was inducted into the team’s “90 greatest” players and coaches list as part of the team’s 90th anniversary.

Since Williams landed with San Francisco, he’s had a rejuvenated his career and has been a three-time consecutive first-team All-Pro from 2021-2023.

He’s also remained a constant at the left tackle position, as he’s appeared in 75 games for the 49ers, including last season where he started in 16 games.

Despite being 38 years old, Williams has been playing at a high level this season alongside the rest of the San Francisco offensive line as quarterback Brock Purdy has been sacked only three times this season. All three of which came last week.

The 49ers enter their Week 6 game against the Commanders with a 5-0 record and are coming off a thrilling 32-29 victory against the Seahawks last week.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Klint Kubiak said changes could be coming as the Raiders searched for answers to their struggling running game.

On Sunday, he followed through.

The Raiders coach benched Jackson Powers-Johnson in favor of Caleb Rogers at right guard to start Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills, turning his talk of potential adjustments into a tangible change along the offensive line.

It”s not known if it’s a full-game benching.

Whether the move produces the desired results remains to be seen. But Kubiak made clear that maintaining the status quo was no longer the only option.

For Powers-Johnson, the decision represents a setback and a challenge to work his way back into the lineup. For Rogers, it presents an opportunity to help address a problem that has made life considerably more difficult for the Raiders’ offense.

The running game is supposed to provide the foundation for Kubiak’s system, creating manageable down-and-distance situations and helping set up opportunities through the air. When it stalls, the effects extend well beyond the rushing totals.

Longer third downs. Fewer favorable situations for the quarterback. More chances for opposing defenses to dictate how possessions unfold.

Changing one player does not guarantee those problems disappear. Nor does benching Powers-Johnson mean the responsibility falls entirely on his shoulders. Effective run blocking requires coordination across the front, with execution and timing extending to everyone involved in the play.

But the switch underscores Kubiak’s willingness to try a different combination rather than simply wait for improvement.

Against Buffalo, the Raiders needed an offense capable of sustaining possessions and giving itself a chance to keep pace. Finding traction on the ground would help accomplish both.

Rogers now gets his chance to contribute to that effort.

The larger question is whether a different face at right guard can help produce a different result for the running game.

Kubiak had promised to consider changes. Sunday brought evidence that he meant it.

news.originalContent:

Tennessee earned its first win of the season in Indianapolis and did so without cornerback Alontae Taylor.

The offseason addition was on the sideline for Sunday’s 26-20 win over the Colts (2-4) due to a coach’s decision and not an injury.

Taylor has been critical for the Titans’ defense, playing 99.7% of defensive snaps in the Titans’ first five games of the season. He signed a three-year, $58 million contract ($42 million guaranteed) in March and has 19 tackles and one sack on the year.

The Titans (1-5) focused on upgradingtheirs secondary by adding Taylor and signing free agent cornerback Cor’Dale Flott to a three-year, $45 million deal.

Veteran free agent addition Josh Williams, who signed a two-year, $8 million contract in March, started in Taylor’s place, returning from injured reserve Saturday. Cornerback Isaiah Oliver was given the game-day elevation from the practice squad.

Tennessee’s secondary hasn’t been productive under new head coach Robert Saleh. The Titans so far only have three interceptions this season. Despite the low takeaways, Tennessee ranked 14th in passing yards allowed per game in the NFL (217.8) coming into the game.

The Titans were also without starting safety Kevin Winston Jr. due to a quad injury against the Colts.

Tennessee may be evenly matched against a Colts squad that has been bombarded with injuries at wide receiver.

The Colts will still be without recently extended Alec Pierce, who’s on the injury reserve with a left heel injury, and second-year tight end Tyler Warren is inactive with a groin injury.

The Titans earned their first division win since November 2024 with a victory on Sunday.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

At this point, somebody might want to check whether the Los Angeles Rams’ special teams unit was built on an ancient burial ground.

Because whatever curse has been haunting the Rams’ kicking game apparently followed their newest kicker straight onto the field Sunday afternoon.

Blake Grupe, making his Rams debut after replacing Harrison Mevis earlier this week, drilled a 44-yard field goal to give Los Angeles an early 3-0 lead over the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium.

Seconds later, he was being helped off the field with a knee injury.

You can’t make this stuff up.

On the ensuing kickoff, Arizona returner Devin Duvernay broke through the Rams’ coverage unit, leaving Grupe as the last line of defense between him and the end zone.

The 5-foot-7, 150-pound kicker managed to force Duvernay out of bounds, saving a potential touchdown. Unfortunately, he injured his knee making the tackle and subsequently headed to the locker room with trainers.

Rams New Kicker Blake Grupe Tried To Tackle Somebody On The Kickoff And Ended Up Injuring Himself.The Rams Just Signed This Guy After Cutting Harrison Mevis.Rough Start. 😬 pic.twitter.com/0BDZRD1hzh

The Rams listed him as doubtful to return.

For the second consecutive game, Los Angeles’ kickoff coverage was so poor that its kicker was forced to make a touchdown-saving tackle.

Last Monday against Buffalo, it was the 6-foot-1, 250-plus-pound Mevis, nicknamed the “Thiccer Kicker,” who pushed the Bills’ returner out of bounds on the opening kickoff.

Mevis subsequently missed two field goals, including a potential overtime game-winner, prompting the Rams to release him Tuesday and sign Grupe off the New York Jets’ practice squad.

Now, after one successful kick, his replacement might be sidelined too.

Rams punter Ethan Evans was spotted practicing field goals on the sideline and could be pressed into emergency duty. If he attempts one, Evans would become the franchise’s ninth different field goal kicker since 2020.

news.originalContent:
President Macron promises to increase security, but stops short of announcing a state of emergency or curfew.

Macron vows action against protest violence after crisis meeting over France unrest

French President Emmanuel Macron has expressed “anger and shame” over what he described as violent protesters’ attempts “to bring down the republic”.

In a televised address to the nation on Sunday, Macron promised that rioters and looters would “pay for their crimes”, after Saturday saw some of the worst urban violence in France in years.

The country’s Interior Ministry said that nearly 2,400 people were arrested on Saturday, with about 1,000 police and gendarmes injured.

Macron said there must be a distinction between protesters with “legitimate demands” and “those who destroyed, smashed, and looted”.

The president pledged to launch a “crisis unit” to provide “urgent aid … for those who are going through difficult moments”. He added that “lessons will be learned” after the destructive violence erupted this weekend.

“We need to be clear: yesterday, our law enforcement officers and officials, despite their professionalism, were subjected to unprecedented violence in several cities,” he said.

“I’ve asked the government to provide all the lessons learned and to be able to anticipate it to make sure that this does not happen again,” Macron said, adding: “We need unity, we need calm and respect.”

Reporting from Paris, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler said Macron’s speech had “perhaps no surprises”.

“Whether it’s going to be enough to placate some people, I’m not really sure, because those who have been out protesting say they’re fed up of hearing these sorts of speeches by the French president,” Butler said.

The protests are quickly becoming a political football for parties vying for public support ahead of presidential elections next year.

Left-wing presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said the French government is “solely responsible” for the destruction during protests, and has “failed to organise the maintenance of public order”.

Far-right presidential hopeful Jordan Bardella called Macron’s Sunday speech “lamentable” and “cowardly”, saying the government has nothing left to offer the French people and “cannot even protect them”.

چرخش ۱۸۰ درجه‌ای توجه این سناتور تقریبا به‌طور کامل نتیجه موج فزاینده مخالفت‌های عمومی بود؛ موجی که سیاستمداران را در سراسر آمریکا وادار کرده برای عقب نماندن از آن دست به کار شوند.

افکار عمومی به‌تدریج علیه گسترش مراکز داده موضع گرفته است؛ ساختمان‌های عظیم و انبارمانندی که توان پردازشی مورد نیاز برای فعالیت‌های اینترنتی را در خود جای می‌دهند.

مراکز داده با ردیف‌های متعدد تراشه‌های رایانه‌ای، که گاهی ارتفاع تجهیزات آن‌ها به بیش از دو متر می‌رسد، دیگر فقط زیرساخت اینترنت نیستند. آن‌ها اکنون به نمود فیزیکی رشد سریع و انفجاری فناوری هوش مصنوعی و نگرانی‌های مختلفی تبدیل شده‌اند که مردم با آن مرتبط می‌دانند.

آنجلیتا سوریانو، ساکن ایندیانا، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «نمی‌خواهم موش آزمایشگاهی این ماجرا باشم.»

درست روبه‌روی خانه او، آمازون در حال ساخت یک مرکز داده جدید است. پس از تکمیل، این مجموعه متشکل از ۲۶ ساختمان بیش از ۲ کیلومتر مربع از محله محل زندگی او را در بر خواهد گرفت و ۷۸۲ ژنراتور دیزلی در آن به کار گرفته خواهد شد.

برخی مراکز داده حتی بزرگ‌ترند.

در اوهایو، پروژه مشترکی میان اوپن‌ای‌آی، انویدیا، اس‌بی انرژی و وزارت انرژی آمریکا قرار است مجموعه‌ای از مراکز داده بسازد که حدود شش مایل مربع، نزدیک به ۱۵/۵ کیلومتر مربع، وسعت خواهد داشت، تقریبا به اندازه بسیاری از شهرک‌های آمریکا.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اکنون حدود ۳ هزار مرکز داده در آمریکا فعال است و بر اساس گزارشی از مرکز پژوهشی پیو، این تعداد ممکن است طی چند سال آینده دو برابر شود.

ساخت مراکز داده عمدتا بر اساس مقررات و مجوزهای محلی انجام می‌شود، بنابراین قانون‌گذاران فدرال مانند سناتورهای آمریکا نقش محدودی در این روند دارند.

اما مخالفت با آن‌ها در آمریکا آن‌قدر سریع و شدید افزایش یافته که حالا سیاستمداران در همه سطوح تقریبا ناچارند موضعی مشخص اتخاذ کنند.

کلویی آتیو، مشاور سیاست‌گذاری هوش مصنوعی، گفت: «این فقط مسئله‌ای مربوط به جناح چپ نیست. در میان محافظه‌کاران هم مخالفت بسیار زیادی با مراکز داده وجود دارد. در هر دو حزب، هر کسی که موضع روشنی بیان کند و به آن پایبند بماند، می‌تواند از نظر سیاسی از آن بهره ببرد.»

مشاور سناتور آمریکایی که روی قانون‌گذاری مراکز داده کار می‌کند نیز ارزیابی مشابهی داشت.

او گفت: «اینجا نیاز مشخصی به سیاست‌گذاری وجود دارد و ما می‌خواهیم این خلا را پر کنیم. مخالفت بزرگی در سراسر کشور شکل گرفته است، مردم آثار مراکز داده را می‌بینند و از آن خوششان نمی‌آید.»

همین موضوع بسیاری از سیاستمداران کنگره، حتی جمهوری‌خواهان، را مستقیما در برابر دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، قرار داده است؛ کسی که از رشد بدون محدودیت فناوری هوش مصنوعی حمایت کرده است.

ترامپ مخالفت با مراکز داده را «توطئه‌ای بیمارگونه» توصیف کرده و گفته است مردم و شهرهایی که می‌کوشند مانع ساخت آن‌ها شوند «عقب‌مانده و فقیر» هستند.

این موضع ترامپ برای سیاستمداران دموکراتی که می‌خواهند در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آرای شهروندان ناراضی یا مردد را جلب کنند، به فرصتی سیاسی تبدیل شده است.

بی‌بی‌سی با ساکنانی از ایندیانا، آریزونا، میشیگان، پنسیلوانیا و اورگن صحبت کرده است که همگی در سطح محلی علیه توسعه مراکز داده فعالیت می‌کنند.

آن‌ها نگرانی‌های مختلفی درباره این ساختمان‌ها مطرح کردند، از جمله اندازه آن‌ها، سروصدای ساخت‌وساز و فعالیت روزانه، اثر بر منابع هوا، آب و انرژی و همچنین سرعتی که به نظر می‌رسد مقام‌های محلی با آن پروژه‌ها را تصویب می‌کنند.

بر اساس پژوهش مؤسسه «دیتا سنتر واچ»، در چند ماه نخست سال جاری شمار گروه‌های محلی که علیه گسترش مراکز داده سازماندهی می‌کنند، بیش از دو برابر شد و به ۸۳۳ گروه رسید؛ گروه‌هایی که اکنون تقریبا در همه ایالت‌های آمریکا فعال‌اند.

«دیتا سنتر واچ» داده‌هایی را برای بازیگران صنعت هوش مصنوعی جمع‌آوری می‌کند و بخشی از شرکت نوپای هوش مصنوعی «۱۰ای لبز» (10a Labs) به شمار می‌رود.

استفانی مالدونادو، مدیر سیاسی سازمان «لوچا»، یک گروه سازمان‌دهی اجتماعی مستقر در ایالت آریزونا، مخالفت‌ها با گسترش مراکز داده را به داستان «داوود و جالوت» تشبیه می‌کند؛ جنبشی که به گفته او چند سال پیش آغاز شد.

مالدونادو افزود: «مردم از مدت‌ها پیش آماده بودند جلو آن را بگیرند. حالا عصبانی‌اند.»

نظرسنجی ملی تازه‌ای نشان می‌دهد پس از جنگ جاری ایران و مسائل مختلف اقتصادی، مقررات هوش مصنوعی و مراکز داده از جمله موضوعات مهم برای رای‌دهندگان در این دوره انتخاباتی هستند.

طرفداران ساخت مراکز داده اغلب می‌گویند این پروژه‌ها شغل‌های بیشتر و با درآمد بالاتر برای جوامع محلی ایجاد می‌کنند.

اما پژوهش تازه موسسه بروکینگز، یک مرکز پژوهشی غیرحزبی، نشان داده است یک مرکز داده جدید بین ۱۰۰ تا ۲۰۰ شغل محلی ایجاد می‌کند؛ رقمی که به گفته این موسسه «کمتر از چیزی است که حامیان صنعت ادعا می‌کنند».

این پروژه‌ها همچنین عملا تاثیری بر سطح دستمزدهای محلی ندارند.

منبع تصویر، Stephanie Maldonado

کتی هابز، فرماندار آریزونا، زمانی از حامیان چنین پروژه‌هایی بود، اما فشار عمومی باعث شد موضع خود را تغییر دهد.

او در ماه ژوئیه یک توقف سه‌ ساله برای اعطای هرگونه معافیت مالیاتی جدید به شرکت‌ها برای پروژه‌های مراکز داده تصویب کرد.

آریزونا تنها ایالتی نیست که سیاستمدارانش در واکنش به مخالفت عمومی با مراکز داده موضع خود را تغییر داده‌اند.

عبدال السید، نامزد دموکرات سنا در میشیگان، وضع مقررات جدید برای مراکز داده را به بخشی روشن از کارزار موفق خود در انتخابات مقدماتی سنا تبدیل کرده است.

در رقابت برای فرمانداری جورجیا نیز یک نامزد دموکرات که خواستار توقف توسعه مراکز داده است، در نظرسنجی‌ها رقابتی بسیار نزدیک با نامزد جمهوری‌خواهی دارد که با چنین توقفی مخالف است.

جان هوستد، سناتور جمهوری‌خواه اوهایو، که برای حفظ کرسی خود در برابر شرود براون، نامزد دموکرات، رقابت می‌کند نیز مجبور شده موضعش را تغییر دهد.

نظرسنجی‌های اخیر نشان داده‌اند اکثریت رای‌دهندگان اوهایو، فارغ از وابستگی حزبی، با مراکز داده مخالف‌اند.

هوستد حمایت خود را تعدیل کرده و گفته است تصمیم درباره ورود این مراکز باید بر عهده شهروندان محلی و مقام‌های منتخب باشد.

در مقابل، براون در کارزار انتخاباتی خود بر مخالفت با مراکز داده جدید تاکید کرده است. در نظرسنجی‌های اخیر او از هوستد جلوتر بوده است.

مشکلات هوستد در اوهایو باعث شد «کمیته ملی سناتوری جمهوری‌خواهان»، یکی از مهم‌ترین نهادهای جذب کمک مالی برای جمهوری‌خواهان سنا، در یادداشتی خصوصی بنویسد که سیاستمداران جمهوری‌خواه باید نحوه صحبت با رای‌دهندگان درباره مراکز داده را کاملا بازتعریف کنند.

این کمیته افزود: «این موضوع به یکی از مسائل کمتر دیده‌شده اما مهم کل چرخه انتخاباتی تبدیل شده است.»

تگزاس شاید روشن‌ترین نمونه‌ای باشد که نشان می‌دهد مخالفت عمومی چگونه حتی برای سیاستمداران به‌شدت طرفدار کسب‌وکار به موضوعی اجتناب‌ناپذیر تبدیل شده است.

بر اساس داده‌های پیو، اکنون نزدیک به ۳۰۰ مرکز داده در این ایالت فعال‌اند و ۱۷۰ مرکز دیگر نیز برای ساخت برنامه‌ریزی شده‌اند.

گرگ ابوت، فرماندار جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، در پایان سال گذشته با افتخار گفته بود تگزاس به دلیل تعداد مراکز داده خود «مرکز توسعه هوش مصنوعی» است.

اما تنها چند ماه بعد عقب‌نشینی کرد و به نگرانی‌هایی درباره «ایمنی و کیفیت زندگی» اشاره کرد.

این مسئله ممکن است در رقابت پیش‌روی سنا در این ایالت نیز نقش داشته باشد.

کارزار جیمز تالاریکو، نامزد دموکرات، خواستار پایان دادن به «توافق‌های مالیاتی ویژه» برای شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری است.

او اکنون در رقابت برای کرسی‌ که از نظر تاریخی در اختیار جمهوری‌خواهان بوده، در برابر کن پکستون، دادستان کل جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، قرار دارد.

پکستون در مصاحبه‌ای در اواخر سپتامبر گفت هنوز «فضای باز فراوانی در تگزاس وجود دارد که می‌توانیم مراکز داده را آنجا بسازیم».

بسیاری از اقدامات یا پیشنهادهایی که سیاستمداران برای پاسخ به نگرانی این رای‌دهندگان مطرح کرده‌اند، موقتی هستند.

برای مثال، بیشتر ممنوعیت‌ها یا توقف‌های موقت پس از یک تا سه سال پایان خواهند یافت.

ممکن است تا زمان پایان این توقف‌ها فضای سیاسی تغییر کرده باشد و شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری و هوش مصنوعی دوباره بتوانند مطابق خواسته خود پروژه‌هایشان را پیش ببرند.

اما فعلا احساسات عمومی نسبت به آن‌ها شدید است.

بالاجی تاماباتولا، مدیرعامل «باراپان» در حال توسعه یک مرکز داده و مجموعه فناوری در زمینی به وسعت به ۷۰۰ جریب در لیبرتی تگزاس است.

او به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که با وجود آنکه این تاسیسات به گونه‌ای طراحی شده‌اند که آب مورد نیاز خود را از طریق جمع‌آوری آب باران تامین کنند و انرژی مورد نیازشان را نیز خود تولید کنند، که رویکردی روزبه‌روز رایج‌تر در پروژه‌های بزرگ مراکز داده است، بسیاری از ساکنان منطقه از همان ابتدا با این طرح مخالفت کرده‌اند.

او گفت: «از همان لحظه اول سطح تنش آن‌قدر بالاست که تقریبا حتی نمی‌توان با ارائه واقعیت‌ها از این دیوار عبور کرد.»

تاماباتولا گفت در یک نشست اجتماعی اخیر تلاش کرده است با زنی که به‌شدت با پروژه مخالف بود، رو‌در‌رو صحبت کند.

او گفت: این زن مستقیم در چشمانم نگاه کرد و گفت: «"از ایالت من برو بیرون."»

اما مخالفت با آن‌ها در آمریکا آن‌قدر سریع و شدید افزایش یافته که حالا سیاستمداران در همه سطوح تقریبا ناچارند موضعی مشخص اتخاذ کنند.

کلویی آتیو، مشاور سیاست‌گذاری هوش مصنوعی، گفت: «این فقط مسئله‌ای مربوط به جناح چپ نیست. در میان محافظه‌کاران هم مخالفت بسیار زیادی با مراکز داده وجود دارد. در هر دو حزب، هر کسی که موضع روشنی بیان کند و به آن پایبند بماند، می‌تواند از نظر سیاسی از آن بهره ببرد.»

مشاور سناتور آمریکایی که روی قانون‌گذاری مراکز داده کار می‌کند نیز ارزیابی مشابهی داشت.

او گفت: «اینجا نیاز مشخصی به سیاست‌گذاری وجود دارد و ما می‌خواهیم این خلا را پر کنیم. مخالفت بزرگی در سراسر کشور شکل گرفته است، مردم آثار مراکز داده را می‌بینند و از آن خوششان نمی‌آید.»

همین موضوع بسیاری از سیاستمداران کنگره، حتی جمهوری‌خواهان، را مستقیما در برابر دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، قرار داده است؛ کسی که از رشد بدون محدودیت فناوری هوش مصنوعی حمایت کرده است.

ترامپ مخالفت با مراکز داده را «توطئه‌ای بیمارگونه» توصیف کرده و گفته است مردم و شهرهایی که می‌کوشند مانع ساخت آن‌ها شوند «عقب‌مانده و فقیر» هستند.

این موضع ترامپ برای سیاستمداران دموکراتی که می‌خواهند در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آرای شهروندان ناراضی یا مردد را جلب کنند، به فرصتی سیاسی تبدیل شده است.

بی‌بی‌سی با ساکنانی از ایندیانا، آریزونا، میشیگان، پنسیلوانیا و اورگن صحبت کرده است که همگی در سطح محلی علیه توسعه مراکز داده فعالیت می‌کنند.

آن‌ها نگرانی‌های مختلفی درباره این ساختمان‌ها مطرح کردند، از جمله اندازه آن‌ها، سروصدای ساخت‌وساز و فعالیت روزانه، اثر بر منابع هوا، آب و انرژی و همچنین سرعتی که به نظر می‌رسد مقام‌های محلی با آن پروژه‌ها را تصویب می‌کنند.

بر اساس پژوهش مؤسسه «دیتا سنتر واچ»، در چند ماه نخست سال جاری شمار گروه‌های محلی که علیه گسترش مراکز داده سازماندهی می‌کنند، بیش از دو برابر شد و به ۸۳۳ گروه رسید؛ گروه‌هایی که اکنون تقریبا در همه ایالت‌های آمریکا فعال‌اند.

«دیتا سنتر واچ» داده‌هایی را برای بازیگران صنعت هوش مصنوعی جمع‌آوری می‌کند و بخشی از شرکت نوپای هوش مصنوعی «۱۰ای لبز» (10a Labs) به شمار می‌رود.

استفانی مالدونادو، مدیر سیاسی سازمان «لوچا»، یک گروه سازمان‌دهی اجتماعی مستقر در ایالت آریزونا، مخالفت‌ها با گسترش مراکز داده را به داستان «داوود و جالوت» تشبیه می‌کند؛ جنبشی که به گفته او چند سال پیش آغاز شد.

مالدونادو افزود: «مردم از مدت‌ها پیش آماده بودند جلو آن را بگیرند. حالا عصبانی‌اند.»

نظرسنجی ملی تازه‌ای نشان می‌دهد پس از جنگ جاری ایران و مسائل مختلف اقتصادی، مقررات هوش مصنوعی و مراکز داده از جمله موضوعات مهم برای رای‌دهندگان در این دوره انتخاباتی هستند.

طرفداران ساخت مراکز داده اغلب می‌گویند این پروژه‌ها شغل‌های بیشتر و با درآمد بالاتر برای جوامع محلی ایجاد می‌کنند.

اما پژوهش تازه موسسه بروکینگز، یک مرکز پژوهشی غیرحزبی، نشان داده است یک مرکز داده جدید بین ۱۰۰ تا ۲۰۰ شغل محلی ایجاد می‌کند؛ رقمی که به گفته این موسسه «کمتر از چیزی است که حامیان صنعت ادعا می‌کنند».

این پروژه‌ها همچنین عملا تاثیری بر سطح دستمزدهای محلی ندارند.

منبع تصویر، Stephanie Maldonado

کتی هابز، فرماندار آریزونا، زمانی از حامیان چنین پروژه‌هایی بود، اما فشار عمومی باعث شد موضع خود را تغییر دهد.

او در ماه ژوئیه یک توقف سه‌ ساله برای اعطای هرگونه معافیت مالیاتی جدید به شرکت‌ها برای پروژه‌های مراکز داده تصویب کرد.

آریزونا تنها ایالتی نیست که سیاستمدارانش در واکنش به مخالفت عمومی با مراکز داده موضع خود را تغییر داده‌اند.

عبدال السید، نامزد دموکرات سنا در میشیگان، وضع مقررات جدید برای مراکز داده را به بخشی روشن از کارزار موفق خود در انتخابات مقدماتی سنا تبدیل کرده است.

در رقابت برای فرمانداری جورجیا نیز یک نامزد دموکرات که خواستار توقف توسعه مراکز داده است، در نظرسنجی‌ها رقابتی بسیار نزدیک با نامزد جمهوری‌خواهی دارد که با چنین توقفی مخالف است.

جان هوستد، سناتور جمهوری‌خواه اوهایو، که برای حفظ کرسی خود در برابر شرود براون، نامزد دموکرات، رقابت می‌کند نیز مجبور شده موضعش را تغییر دهد.

نظرسنجی‌های اخیر نشان داده‌اند اکثریت رای‌دهندگان اوهایو، فارغ از وابستگی حزبی، با مراکز داده مخالف‌اند.

هوستد حمایت خود را تعدیل کرده و گفته است تصمیم درباره ورود این مراکز باید بر عهده شهروندان محلی و مقام‌های منتخب باشد.

در مقابل، براون در کارزار انتخاباتی خود بر مخالفت با مراکز داده جدید تاکید کرده است. در نظرسنجی‌های اخیر او از هوستد جلوتر بوده است.

مشکلات هوستد در اوهایو باعث شد «کمیته ملی سناتوری جمهوری‌خواهان»، یکی از مهم‌ترین نهادهای جذب کمک مالی برای جمهوری‌خواهان سنا، در یادداشتی خصوصی بنویسد که سیاستمداران جمهوری‌خواه باید نحوه صحبت با رای‌دهندگان درباره مراکز داده را کاملا بازتعریف کنند.

این کمیته افزود: «این موضوع به یکی از مسائل کمتر دیده‌شده اما مهم کل چرخه انتخاباتی تبدیل شده است.»

تگزاس شاید روشن‌ترین نمونه‌ای باشد که نشان می‌دهد مخالفت عمومی چگونه حتی برای سیاستمداران به‌شدت طرفدار کسب‌وکار به موضوعی اجتناب‌ناپذیر تبدیل شده است.

بر اساس داده‌های پیو، اکنون نزدیک به ۳۰۰ مرکز داده در این ایالت فعال‌اند و ۱۷۰ مرکز دیگر نیز برای ساخت برنامه‌ریزی شده‌اند.

گرگ ابوت، فرماندار جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، در پایان سال گذشته با افتخار گفته بود تگزاس به دلیل تعداد مراکز داده خود «مرکز توسعه هوش مصنوعی» است.

اما تنها چند ماه بعد عقب‌نشینی کرد و به نگرانی‌هایی درباره «ایمنی و کیفیت زندگی» اشاره کرد.

این مسئله ممکن است در رقابت پیش‌روی سنا در این ایالت نیز نقش داشته باشد.

کارزار جیمز تالاریکو، نامزد دموکرات، خواستار پایان دادن به «توافق‌های مالیاتی ویژه» برای شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری است.

او اکنون در رقابت برای کرسی‌ که از نظر تاریخی در اختیار جمهوری‌خواهان بوده، در برابر کن پکستون، دادستان کل جمهوری‌خواه تگزاس، قرار دارد.

پکستون در مصاحبه‌ای در اواخر سپتامبر گفت هنوز «فضای باز فراوانی در تگزاس وجود دارد که می‌توانیم مراکز داده را آنجا بسازیم».

بسیاری از اقدامات یا پیشنهادهایی که سیاستمداران برای پاسخ به نگرانی این رای‌دهندگان مطرح کرده‌اند، موقتی هستند.

برای مثال، بیشتر ممنوعیت‌ها یا توقف‌های موقت پس از یک تا سه سال پایان خواهند یافت.

ممکن است تا زمان پایان این توقف‌ها فضای سیاسی تغییر کرده باشد و شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری و هوش مصنوعی دوباره بتوانند مطابق خواسته خود پروژه‌هایشان را پیش ببرند.

اما فعلا احساسات عمومی نسبت به آن‌ها شدید است.

بالاجی تاماباتولا، مدیرعامل «باراپان» در حال توسعه یک مرکز داده و مجموعه فناوری در زمینی به وسعت به ۷۰۰ جریب در لیبرتی تگزاس است.

او به بی‌بی‌سی گفت که با وجود آنکه این تاسیسات به گونه‌ای طراحی شده‌اند که آب مورد نیاز خود را از طریق جمع‌آوری آب باران تامین کنند و انرژی مورد نیازشان را نیز خود تولید کنند، که رویکردی روزبه‌روز رایج‌تر در پروژه‌های بزرگ مراکز داده است، بسیاری از ساکنان منطقه از همان ابتدا با این طرح مخالفت کرده‌اند.

او گفت: «از همان لحظه اول سطح تنش آن‌قدر بالاست که تقریبا حتی نمی‌توان با ارائه واقعیت‌ها از این دیوار عبور کرد.»

تاماباتولا گفت در یک نشست اجتماعی اخیر تلاش کرده است با زنی که به‌شدت با پروژه مخالف بود، رو‌در‌رو صحبت کند.

او گفت: این زن مستقیم در چشمانم نگاه کرد و گفت: «"از ایالت من برو بیرون."»

news.originalContent:
A government at war with its critics – from young protesters to the media.

A wave of youth-led protests has returned to the streets of India’s capital, Delhi, after media reports revealed that the Electoral Commission removed about 130 million names from voter lists.

These protests differ from the unrest that exploded in July, though, by the attacks on the media.

Dozens of journalists and content creators have been detained, assaulted or blocked from doing their jobs. But tightening the screws on critical reporting doesn’t appear to be working, as a new generation rises to challenge the government.

Contributors:
Saba Naqvi – Author and journalist
Smita Sharma – Multimedia journalist
Shyam Meera Singh – Founder, Strike Originals
Sushant Singh – Lecturer, Yale University

Pakistan has declared a state of emergency in the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, following protests calling for the release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan.

The state’s response has followed a familiar pattern: A media blackout and internet shutdown, while casting protesters as rebels.

It’s been more than three years since Jair Bolsonaro fell from power, yet the right-wing movement he started is still without a clear leader. Into that gap has stepped a new crop of young evangelical political influencers, who are tapping into a decades-old religious media machine to build their audience.

Their viral content ricochets across social feeds, mobilising followers and voters in ways old-school politicians just can’t match.

The Listening Post’s Nicholas Muirhead reports on Brazil’s evangelical influencers and the political space they are looking to take over.

Featuring: 
Anna Virginia Balloussier – Journalist, Folha De Sao Paulo
Caro Evangelista – Executive director, Iser
Magali Cunha – Editor-in-chief, Berreia Project

news.originalContent:
Demonstrations are spreading across the continent.

Weeks of student protests in France have grown into some of the worst unrest in Europe in recent years.

The demonstrations started as a call for reforms to the education system. But they have since expanded into protests against the high cost of living and planned cuts to social services.

And France is not alone. Demonstrators have taken to the streets in other parts of Europe. They are venting their frustrations against leaders they say have failed to address their needs, and putting pressure on their governments.

And right-wing parties are looking to seize the moment to make political gains.

Diane De Vignemont – Independent journalist and historian

Julius Fintelmann – Co-founder and editor-in-chief at The European Correspondent

Jaime Velazquez – Independent journalist who specialises in the political landscape in Spain

Ukraine’s president says communication between Washington and Kyiv ‘virtually nonstop’, despite a spat with Trump.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that the war with Russia “must be brought to an end” and that his country is preparing for the “next steps” of diplomacy to end the conflict.

Zelenskyy said on X on Sunday that he had a “conversation with the American president’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner”. He added that “a lot depends” on the US position, but it’s clear there are “many things that matter to all of us”.

The Ukrainian leader’s comments come amid a significant diplomatic fallout with US President Donald Trump, who on Saturday waived expected sanctions targeting Russia’s energy economy and previously called renewed Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure “a disgrace”.

Nonetheless, Zelenskyy said his team is in “virtually nonstop communication” with their US counterparts and said a focus of dialogue is on the results of the talks in Florida and further steps.

Also on Sunday, Zelenskyy said he was “thankful” that the US had resumed intelligence sharing with Ukraine after a pause left Ukraine particularly vulnerable to Russia’s regular ballistic missile attacks.

“It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was deblocked by the American side,” Zelenskyy told NBC, adding: “Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days”.

Kyiv has also reported restrictions on the speed of satellite service Starshield, a military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite connectivity network, provided to Ukraine by Musk’s company SpaceX.

Ukraine said its relays were experiencing a limit on how fast receivers could travel while maintaining connectivity, making it almost impossible to intercept Russia’s upgraded jet-powered long-range drones.

Musk had said any restrictions imposed on Starshield connectivity were the responsibility of the US government. The White House quickly rebuked that and in an NBC interview on Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Zelenskyy “very reckless” for accusing the US of throttling connectivity.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that Ukraine is currently blocked from Starshield, and that a request from Kyiv to access the system for attacks deep inside Russia is “under discussion”.

Also on Sunday, Ukrainian media reported that Russian strikes killed two people in the western Volyn region, near the border with Poland, and injured at least five others across the country. Overnight attacks by Russia killed a woman and injured a six-year-old in the Zaporizhzhia region.

On Saturday night and in the early hours of Sunday, Ukraine hit Russia’s second-largest city, St Petersburg, with a significant drone attack. It targeted a key oil refinery and depot, a warehouse of Russian online retailer Ozon and a data centre run by Russian social media company, VKontakte.

At least one person was killed in the attack, which Russian state media said was the largest on the city since the start of the war in 2022.
news.content:
Ukraine’s president says communication between Washington and Kyiv ‘virtually nonstop’, despite a spat with Trump.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that the war with Russia “must be brought to an end” and that his country is preparing for the “next steps” of diplomacy to end the conflict.

Zelenskyy said on X on Sunday that he had a “conversation with the American president’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner”. He added that “a lot depends” on the US position, but it’s clear there are “many things that matter to all of us”.

The Ukrainian leader’s comments come amid a significant diplomatic fallout with US President Donald Trump, who on Saturday waived expected sanctions targeting Russia’s energy economy and previously called renewed Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure “a disgrace”.

Nonetheless, Zelenskyy said his team is in “virtually nonstop communication” with their US counterparts and said a focus of dialogue is on the results of the talks in Florida and further steps.

Also on Sunday, Zelenskyy said he was “thankful” that the US had resumed intelligence sharing with Ukraine after a pause left Ukraine particularly vulnerable to Russia’s regular ballistic missile attacks.

“It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was deblocked by the American side,” Zelenskyy told NBC, adding: “Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days”.

Kyiv has also reported restrictions on the speed of satellite service Starshield, a military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite connectivity network, provided to Ukraine by Musk’s company SpaceX.

Ukraine said its relays were experiencing a limit on how fast receivers could travel while maintaining connectivity, making it almost impossible to intercept Russia’s upgraded jet-powered long-range drones.

Musk had said any restrictions imposed on Starshield connectivity were the responsibility of the US government. The White House quickly rebuked that and in an NBC interview on Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Zelenskyy “very reckless” for accusing the US of throttling connectivity.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that Ukraine is currently blocked from Starshield, and that a request from Kyiv to access the system for attacks deep inside Russia is “under discussion”.

Also on Sunday, Ukrainian media reported that Russian strikes killed two people in the western Volyn region, near the border with Poland, and injured at least five others across the country. Overnight attacks by Russia killed a woman and injured a six-year-old in the Zaporizhzhia region.

On Saturday night and in the early hours of Sunday, Ukraine hit Russia’s second-largest city, St Petersburg, with a significant drone attack. It targeted a key oil refinery and depot, a warehouse of Russian online retailer Ozon and a data centre run by Russian social media company, VKontakte.

At least one person was killed in the attack, which Russian state media said was the largest on the city since the start of the war in 2022.

news.originalContent:
Image not from story(Photo by Chris Hondros/Getty Images)

A Catholic priest in Ecuador was killed when a crucifix broke loose from the wall and fell on him during a Mass he was streaming live.

Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was leading a service on Saturday, Oct. 17, at Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church in Guayaquil when the heavy cross gave way, according to Newsweek. The fixture tore loose about 27 minutes into the online broadcast.

The wooden cross had hung on the wall behind the altar. Footage of the Mass captured it toppling onto the priest as he spoke to worshippers. Congregants rushed forward to help him. He died from his injuries.

The cause of the collapse remained unknown, Newsweek reported. No official statement had said whether structural damage or faulty fittings contributed. (RELATED: Rider’s Fatal Fall Captured In Rollercoaster Souvenir Photo: REPORT)

The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed the priest’s death in a post on social media on Sunday. The archdiocese said he had passed into God’s presence and asked that he be granted eternal rest. It also sent condolences to his family and to his Redemptorist community.

Sánchez Molinari served as parish priest of Our Lady of Perpetual Help in the city’s Central Vicariate, according to Newsweek. He belonged to the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, the order widely known as the Redemptorists. He streamed his Masses regularly through his own social media accounts and a YouTube channel. Earlier in his ministry he had worked in Vinces, in Los Ríos Province, according to Newseek, citing Guayaquil News.

The Italian priest St. Alphonsus Liguori founded the Redemptorist order in 1732. The congregation has long concentrated its work among poor and isolated communities. Its members now total roughly 4,500 across 82 countries.

By Sunday, the church had still offered no public account of what caused the fall, according to IBTimes.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Amir Levy/Getty Images)

Israeli officials reportedly urged Qatar for years to keep sending money into Hamas-controlled Gaza.

Letters top Israeli security officials sent to Qatari leaders show Israel pushed for and helped run a program which moved close to $2 billion into Gaza, TIME reported Sunday. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is running in Israel’s Oct. 27 national elections and was endorsed Sunday by President Donald Trump, has tried to distance himself from the payments, according to the outlet.

Letters obtained by TIME reveal Israel played a bigger role in the payments than Netanyahu has acknowledged.https://t.co/M1oyRf1mFl

Then-Mossad Director Yossi Cohen thanked Qatar’s emir, Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in a 2020 letter for the “humanitarian aid efforts that the State of Qatar has provided the last few years to the Gaza Strip,” according to the outlet.

“Undoubtedly, these humanitarian efforts have played a crucial role in improving the humanitarian situation within the Gaza Strip, and ensuring stability and safety in the region,” Cohen wrote.

That same year, R. L. Maoz, who served on Netanyahu’s National Security Council, urged Qatari officials to keep the payments going even as the Israeli government criticized them in public, according to the outlet. “We reiterate the importance of continuing to transfer the Qatari humanitarian financial assistance through the existing mechanism,” Maoz wrote. (RELATED: Israeli Opposition Accuses Netanyahu Of Being Too Pro-Palestine)

Neither the Embassy of Israel in the United States nor the State of Qatar’s International Media Office immediately responded to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s requests for comment.

Then-Mossad Director David Barnea met with Qatari officials in September 2023, weeks before Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel, The New York Times reported in December 2023, citing several people familiar with the talks. Asked whether Israel wanted the payments to continue, Barnea responded affirmatively, according to the outlet.

While Netanyahu’s office did not respond to a request for comment from TIME, he told the outlet in 2024 the payments were intended to keep Gaza from collapsing. “The reason that successive governments agreed to that is that we wanted to make sure that Gaza has a functioning civilian administration to avoid humanitarian collapse,” he said.

A spokesperson for Qatar’s International Media Office, meanwhile, told TIME that all of the country’s aid went through Israel on its way into Gaza. “If any funding reached Hamas, as alleged by individuals and groups with political agendas against Qatar, the responsibility lies with Israel, which oversaw the delivery and created the mechanism,” the spokesperson reportedly said.

Qatar and several other Arab nations are working with Trump administration envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on a plan to restore Gaza’s basic services and end its reliance on armed Islamist groups, TIME reported.

news.originalSummary:

news.originalContent:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Sunday when NBC News’ Kristen Welker asked why President Donald Trump is “rewarding a dictator” by waiving Russia sanctions.

Bessent said on “Meet the Press” that no sanctions were lifted and that European countries are still paying Russia for its energy. Trump effectively waived a law that would have added more sanctions, Bessent said, and the only thing lifted was the embargo on Russian diesel.

“No one has been tougher on Russian sanctions than President Trump,” Bessent said, pointing to Trump’s sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil, Russia’s two largest energy companies. (RELATED: ‘No, We Haven’t’: Chris Wright Fires Back When Asked If Trump Admin Let Americans Down At Pump)

“But you then are pushing for even tougher sanctions,” Welker countered.

“But Kristen, we did the toughest sanctions,” the secretary said as he and the NBC News host continued to talk over each other.

“But why lift them now. What has [Russian President Vladimir] Putin done to deserve sanctions relief now?” Welker asked.

“Kristen, that’s not true. No sanctions were lifted on Friday,” Bessent insisted. “No sanctions were lifted.”

“There was a law that was supposed to put more sanctions in place. The president effectively waived that,” Welker pointed out.

Trump signed an executive order Friday waiving the Russian sanctions and tariffs required under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which he signed into law Sept. 18.

The law, named for the late Republican South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham, directs the president to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from the top five importers of Russian oil and gas and up to 500 percent on goods imported from Russia. The Senate passed it 86-11 on Aug. 7, and the House passed it 262-159 in September.

Bessent again ensured Welker that “no sanctions were lifted,” and that the “only thing that has been lifted was the diesel embargo.”

Also during the exchange, Welker told Bessent that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had told her the move “is a big support for Putin” and asked, “Why is the president rewarding a dictator who invaded Ukraine?”

“President Trump has made it clear he wants the killing to stop,” Bessent responded, adding that the law gives the president 60 days to assess the situation.

He then turned to Europe, saying European countries have given Russia Putin more money than they have given Ukraine.

“They continue to gorge on Russian energy,” Bessent said. (RELATED: Trump’s Diesel Deal With Putin Runs Into The Ban Congress Passed On Russian Energy)

The secretary said 136 of the 140 cargoes that left one Russian facility in the first six months of the year went to Europe, worth more than $8 billion. He said he asked European allies in the spring to join the U.S. in putting secondary tariffs on China and India and that they refused. “So why should the U.S. bear the burden?” he asked.

Welker then played a clip from Bessent’s January 2025 confirmation hearing, in which he said the Biden administration had been worried about raising U.S. energy prices during an election season. “Is President Trump doing what you accused President Biden of doing?” she asked.

“Kristen, the sanctions were double the Biden administration in an act of incredible bravery,” he replied. “Double the sanctions on the way out in January 2025.”

Bessent also said during the interview that the United Kingdom waived its own embargo on diesel and jet fuel made with Russian crude in May, asking, “where’s the outrage for the rest of the world?”

“The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine,” he added.

news.originalContent:
Image not from story(Photo by ALLISON JOYCE/AFP via Getty Images)

An Air Force airman died Saturday night after losing control during a rappelling demonstration and falling to the field before the UTSA-Navy football game in San Antonio.

Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada confirmed to Task & Purpose that the airman belonged to the 6th Combat Training Squadron, Detachment 2, and died at a hospital from injuries he suffered at the Alamodome. The base withheld his name and said officials have opened an investigation.

The airman was one of four military members scheduled to descend from the stadium rafters roughly 15 minutes ahead of kickoff, ESPN reported, as part of the school’s annual Salute to Armed Forces & Veterans game. He appeared to lose his grip partway down, slid along the rope and struck the turf near midfield. The drop measured about 170 feet. (RELATED: Rider’s Fatal Fall Captured In Rollercoaster Souvenir Photo: REPORT)

Medical crews worked on him for close to 10 minutes before carrying him out and moving him as a Priority 1 patient, Daily Voice reported. KSAT reported that staff surrounded him on the field and that he left the stadium on a golf cart. The Air Force later confirmed he had not survived.

We are deeply saddened by the incident that occurred at the start of tonight’s football game. Our heartfelt thoughts and prayers are with the soldier who was affected, his family and his military colleagues. We recognize that members of our campus community may be emotionally affected by this incident and are activating wellbeing services to support our faculty, staff and students. (1/2)

Fans watched the fall in stunned silence. “Once the band started playing, there was a guy that fell down, and started coming down fast,” witness Adrian Corey told KSAT. “Everybody was quiet, the band stopped performing, everybody was dead silent.”

Another witness, Siomara Corey, told the station, “It was a very sad moment and we don’t know (his condition). There was no updates after that other than asking for prayers, but it did not look good.”

UTSA expressed grief over the accident. “We are deeply saddened by the incident that occurred at the start of tonight’s game,” the university said in a statement. The school opened crisis and counseling services for students and employees shaken by what they saw, KSAT reported. Head coach Jeff Traylor called the scene “heartbreaking” and “tragic,” according to ESPN.

Officials delayed kickoff by 10 minutes and played the game, which UTSA won 38-34, Daily Voice reported.

The 6th Combat Training Squadron prepares service members to become Tactical Air Control Party airmen, terminal air controllers who embed with ground troops and coordinate airstrikes, according to Task & Purpose. The cause of the fall remains unknown.

Parents accused a youth sports travel company of misleading families into paying hotel booking fees and higher lodging costs by telling them their children could not compete unless they booked through its platform, according to a federal lawsuit.

The proposed class action against Team Travel Source challenges “stay-to-play” practices that tie tournament partici
news.originalContent:
Photo by Garry Austin/Getty Images

Parents accused a youth sports travel company of misleading families into paying hotel booking fees and higher lodging costs by telling them their children could not compete unless they booked through its platform, according to a federal lawsuit.

The proposed class action against Team Travel Source challenges “stay-to-play” practices that tie tournament participation to designated hotel booking arrangements, adding to the costs families face beyond registration, equipment and travel. Attorney Karen Dahlberg O’Connell told the Daily Caller News Foundation that hundreds of parents contacted her legal team after the case was filed, reporting similar experiences across the country.

The lawsuit, filed in the Western District of Kentucky against The Complete Plan Inc., which operates as Team Travel Source, includes nine parents from seven states whose children participate in cheerleading and volleyball. The amended complaint alleges deceptive booking requirements, inadequately disclosed mandatory fees and misleading promises of discounted hotel rates.

Team Travel Source denied wrongdoing in a statement provided to the DCNF by Kelley Roberts.

“We deny participation in any alleged violation of the law in connection with the allegations in the proposed class action lawsuit or otherwise,” the company said, adding that it would address the allegations through counsel in the appropriate forum. “We have always run our company in an ethical way and truly appreciate everyone in the space.”

In court filings seeking dismissal, the company argued that tournament organizers established stay-to-play requirements and determine exemptions. It also said its checkout process disclosed fees before customers finalized reservations and that families received services including room blocks, booking assistance and customer support.

Kentucky mother Kate Russell alleged she booked three nights at an Atlanta hotel for $516.85, including $15 in booking service fees, after being told her daughter’s volleyball team could be disqualified if she did not reserve through the platform. A teammate’s family booked elsewhere and the child still competed, according to the complaint.

The parents also challenged mandatory charges labeled as booking, housing, cancellation convenience and premier property fees. Some applied per night even when a parent made a single reservation, the complaint alleges.

The company’s guarantee applies only to some events, excludes booking fees from rate comparisons and requires matching room types, amenities and cancellation terms. Membership and government rates are among its exclusions.

O’Connell described one parent who reported finding a cheaper room directly through a hotel but was denied an adjustment because the Team Travel Source reservation guaranteed access to a rollaway bed. The parent neither wanted nor needed that bed, O’Connell said.

The amended complaint also cites company marketing claiming more than $17 million in rebates paid to tournament organizers in 2025. Plaintiffs allege those payments were funded by inflated lodging costs and fees; that funding allegation remains disputed.

The company’s reach extended to more than 1,600 annual events in over 400 cities across 44 states, according to website figures cited in the complaint.

An Aspen Institute survey found families spent an average of $1,016 on one child’s primary sport in 2024, up 46% from 2019.

“I just want parents to have the freedom of choice in terms of how they stay and where they stay,” O’Connell told the DCNF.

news.content:
Photo by Garry Austin/Getty Images

Parents accused a youth sports travel company of misleading families into paying hotel booking fees and higher lodging costs by telling them their children could not compete unless they booked through its platform, according to a federal lawsuit.

The proposed class action against Team Travel Source challenges “stay-to-play” practices that tie tournament participation to designated hotel booking arrangements, adding to the costs families face beyond registration, equipment and travel. Attorney Karen Dahlberg O’Connell told the Daily Caller News Foundation that hundreds of parents contacted her legal team after the case was filed, reporting similar experiences across the country.

The lawsuit, filed in the Western District of Kentucky against The Complete Plan Inc., which operates as Team Travel Source, includes nine parents from seven states whose children participate in cheerleading and volleyball. The amended complaint alleges deceptive booking requirements, inadequately disclosed mandatory fees and misleading promises of discounted hotel rates.

Team Travel Source denied wrongdoing in a statement provided to the DCNF by Kelley Roberts.

“We deny participation in any alleged violation of the law in connection with the allegations in the proposed class action lawsuit or otherwise,” the company said, adding that it would address the allegations through counsel in the appropriate forum. “We have always run our company in an ethical way and truly appreciate everyone in the space.”

In court filings seeking dismissal, the company argued that tournament organizers established stay-to-play requirements and determine exemptions. It also said its checkout process disclosed fees before customers finalized reservations and that families received services including room blocks, booking assistance and customer support.

Kentucky mother Kate Russell alleged she booked three nights at an Atlanta hotel for $516.85, including $15 in booking service fees, after being told her daughter’s volleyball team could be disqualified if she did not reserve through the platform. A teammate’s family booked elsewhere and the child still competed, according to the complaint.

The parents also challenged mandatory charges labeled as booking, housing, cancellation convenience and premier property fees. Some applied per night even when a parent made a single reservation, the complaint alleges.

The company’s guarantee applies only to some events, excludes booking fees from rate comparisons and requires matching room types, amenities and cancellation terms. Membership and government rates are among its exclusions.

O’Connell described one parent who reported finding a cheaper room directly through a hotel but was denied an adjustment because the Team Travel Source reservation guaranteed access to a rollaway bed. The parent neither wanted nor needed that bed, O’Connell said.

The amended complaint also cites company marketing claiming more than $17 million in rebates paid to tournament organizers in 2025. Plaintiffs allege those payments were funded by inflated lodging costs and fees; that funding allegation remains disputed.

The company’s reach extended to more than 1,600 annual events in over 400 cities across 44 states, according to website figures cited in the complaint.

An Aspen Institute survey found families spent an average of $1,016 on one child’s primary sport in 2024, up 46% from 2019.

“I just want parents to have the freedom of choice in terms of how they stay and where they stay,” O’Connell told the DCNF.

The parents seek class certification, damages and court orders addressing the challenged practices. Team Travel Source asked the court to dismiss the amended complaint and filed its reply supporting that request on Wednesday.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images)

Voters will cast ballots on several ballot initiatives addressing voter identification, abortion, data centers and other issues in the 2026 election cycle.

More than 140 total measures across 40 states plan to touch on some of the most hot-button issues in politics. Several states ranging from Virginia to California are asking voters to decide whether to amend their state constitutions on elections and social issues.

Voters in Idaho, Virginia and Missouri will decide whether to keep or amend their states’ abortion laws. Measures in Virginia and Nevada would enshrine abortion legalization in the states’ constitutions before the point of fetal viability, which happens around 24 weeks of pregnancy.

Question 1 of Virginia’s ballot initiatives would also prevent any laws restricting “personal decisions” about prenatal care, birth control, or postpartum treatment, according to the Virginia Department of Elections. In January, Democratic Virginia state lawmakers advanced a constitutional amendment on abortion rights to appear on the November ballot. (RELATED: Virginia Democrats Want Abortion In The Constitution. 700,000 Catholics Could Stand In Their Way)

Bishop Michael Burbidge of the Diocese of Arlington issued a Sept. 12 letter urging Virginians to join the “Catholics Vote No” campaign and oppose Ballot Questions 1 and 2. The second initiative in Virginia would remove a constitutional ban on same-sex marriage in the event that the Supreme Court overturned Obergefell v. Hodges, which deemed state bans on same-sex marriage unconstitutional.

🚨A RARE MOVE by a Virginia Bishop Ahead of Election Day "Catholic Bishop Michael Burbidge says he has never before asked every priest in his diocese to do what he requested this weekend: read a letter at Mass urging Catholics to oppose two Virginia constitutional amendments on abortion and marriage." "Across 70 parishes serving more than 430,000 Catholics in Northern Virginia, worshippers heard Burbidge warn against what he called ‘two dangerous ballot initiatives’—proposed constitutional amendments that Virginians will decide Nov. 3. Early voting begins Friday." "The effort follows a joint statement Burbidge issued with Richmond Bishop Barry Knestout in August. In his latest letter, Burbidge urged parishioners to pledge to vote at https://t.co/kJzKhv4RZd, cast ballots early beginning Friday, and encourage their family, friends, and colleagues to oppose the amendments." … MORE:⬇️ https://t.co/DdCxpfV172 Video: Statement of Bishop Burbidge Instructing Catholics to Vote ‘No’ on Virginia Ballot Questions 1 & 2

“[Ballot Question 1] threatens the health and safety of mothers and would allow for abortions targeting healthy babies all the way up to birth,” Burbidge’s letter said. “The amendment extends this so-called right even to minors. It would remove the role of parents concerning life-altering and irreversible decisions for their minor daughters.”

“The proposed amendment is extreme. It is unnecessary. And it is wrong,” the letter continues.

Democratic Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger and Democratic Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones expressed support for the two proposed amendments. Catholic parishes across the state, including the Basilica of St. Mary in Alexandria, Virginia, have registered parishioners to vote as part of the “Catholics Say No” campaign.

There are over 693,000 registered Catholic voters in the Dioceses of Arlington and Richmond, according to the Virginia Catholic Conference.

Another ballot initiative in Idaho would overturn the state’s near-total abortion ban and establish a “right” for a woman to have an abortion until viability. Idaho passed legislation in 2020 that outlawed abortions except in cases of rape, incest and life of the mother. Performing abortions outside of those circumstances is punishable by two to five years in prison.

In Missouri, Amendment 3 would repeal the 2024 abortion rights amendment and ban nearly all abortions and trans-related surgeries for minors.

California’s state Legislature introduced Proposition 40, which would institute a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of billionaires to raise tens of billions in revenue to address education services, health, nutrition and other services, according to the California Budget & Policy Center. There is a high degree of uncertainty in estimating the potential revenue from this measure, though the Legislative Analyst’s Office estimated that it would likely raise “tens of millions” of dollars in the near term. It could reduce state income tax collections by roughly $1 billion per year.

The billionaire tax intends to provide financial assistance following the federal and state-level cuts to healthcare, food assistance and K-14 public education programs, according to the California Budget & Policy Center. It would create a special fund, the 2026 Billionaire Tax Reserve Fund, to hold the revenue.

Some individuals expressed concerns about the measure being a one-time tax that would only be available for a few years, according to the California Budget & Policy Center. It would not be available to support other state services and there is uncertainty over how billionaires would respond to the tax.

In Florida, Amendment 3 would add a constitutional amendment to increase the homestead tax exemption for non-school taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, according to Ballotpedia. It would give new Florida residents a smaller initial exemption until they have lived in the state for five years and restrict counties and municipalities to spending property tax revenue on public safety, education, natural resource projects and infrastructure.

A homestead exemption allows homeowners to exempt a portion of its assessed value from property taxes, reducing the amount they owe.

Republican Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis called for a special legislative session in June to consider the constitutional amendment, according to Ballotpedia.

“Property tax revenue collected by local governments has nearly doubled in the past seven years and is expected to reach an astounding $83 billion by 2032,” DeSantis said. “Florida homeowners need relief. Now is the time to stand up for taxpayers, enact a historic reform, and save the home of every Floridian.”

Voters in more than 15 states will decide on measures regarding voting, voter identification and citizenship. Arizona, Arkansas, Kansas, West Virginia and South Dakota are considering amending their constitutions to say that only U.S. citizens could vote in elections.

Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, North Carolina and Ohio will consider amendments requiring specific identification from voters when they vote in-person or by mail. These moves followed the U.S. Senate’s inability to pass the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) America Act, which would require voters to provide proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and present photo identification at the voting booth.

A Fox News poll from July found that the vast majority of Americans, 83%, support identification to register to vote and 77% support it to vote.

Massachusetts voters will consider a new statute to allow same-day voter registration. The state currently requires residents to register to vote at least ten days before Election Day, which some have argued “disenfranchises thousands of voters,” according to MassVote.

Supporters of the amendment argue that same-day registration increases voter turnout, helps election officials and is safe to implement through modern technology. Opponents expressed concerns that verifying a voter’s eligibility could cause disruption and confusion on Election Day.

Democratic Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey endorsed the initiative, arguing that registration should be “easy and automatic,” according to MassLive.

Alaskans will decide whether to repeal a previous ballot measure that enacted ranked-choice voting in 2020 and end the state’s open primary system.

California, Colorado and Nevada would expand laws requiring voters to show identification before voting. Arizona, Ohio and North Carolina would add voter ID requirements into their state constitutions.

In Virginia, voters will consider a constitutional amendment restoring voting rights for convicted felons upon their release from prison. The state is currently one of the hardest states for someone with a felony conviction to earn back their right to vote.

At least 39 data center measures will be on the ballot in eight states. Ohio municipalities will vote on 21 measures related to data centers, including nine petitions that would ban data centers that draw over 25 megawatts of energy per month, according to The Ohio Capital Journal. Other proposals would require hyper-scale data center developers receiving tax incentives to provide financial guarantees.

Two measures in Venice, Illinois, and Nameoki, Illinois, would advise data center construction and operation in the township, according to Ballotpedia. One initiative in Maine would establish a six-month moratorium on applications for new or expanded data centers.

Data centers drove up the costs of electricity, rising 13% in Virginia, 16% in Illinois and 12% in Ohio over a one-year time frame, according to CNBC. Data center construction rose 57% from July 2025 to July while energy costs rose.

Natural gas consumption used to generate electricity for U.S. data centers is projected to increase by 15 billion cubic feet per day through 2035, putting U.S. data centers on track to consume more natural gas than nearly every other country. A New Jersey data center spilled an estimated 5,000 gallons of No. 2 diesel fuel into a nearby creek in September.

Some initiatives would address redistricting, which became a hot button issue in the 2026 midterm cycle. Voters in Missouri will consider whether to repeal new congressional districts passed by the Republican-controlled state Legislature, while an initiative in Colorado would make it harder to redraw congressional districts by requiring any such maps in 2028 to follow a more extensive approval process.

Washington, Arizona, Nebraska and Colorado will vote on whether to ban trans-identifying athletes from participating on sports teams that match their gender identity. Washington and Nebraska’s ballot measures would only apply for men competing on women’s sports, while Arizona’s and Colorado’s would apply to both male and female teams.

Another initiative in Colorado would ban sex change operations and other procedures for minors.

Some states would address education, including in Alabama, which has one proposal that would require public schools to play the national anthem at least once a year. Another would require schools to recite the Pledge of Allegiance daily and mandate school boards to adopt policies that allow student-led prayer.

Arizona and Wisconsin have measures that would ban affirmative action in schools and state government agencies. The Arizona measure, Proposition 142, would amend the state constitution to expand restrictions on preferential treatment, discrimination and diversity policies across the entire state government.

The Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment Amendment in Wisconsin would “prohibit any governmental entity from discriminating or granting preferential treatment based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, public education, public contracting, or public administration,” according to Ballotpedia.

The Supreme Court ruled against race-based admissions in June 2023.
